title: SLO Drift Playbook & Initiative Orchestrator: automated triage -> backlog mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We regularly see gradual SLI drift (latency/availability regressions) that consume error budget over several days without a single obvious root cause. Current playbooks are ad-hoc: on-call pages, large postmortems, and manual conversion of incidents into initiatives. This creates noisy prioritization and slow remediation that hurts customer-facing SLAs.

Goal: Deliver a repeatable, cross-team 'SLO Drift Playbook & Initiative Orchestrator' that detects SLI drift patterns, triages severity, and converts actionable findings into prioritized initiatives or experiments in the initiative backlog. The orchestrator should reduce time-to-action, provide experiment templates (canary throttles, cache warmers, batch tuning), and attach rollback/gating recommendations to feature rollouts.

Scope:
- Define drift detection thresholds and classification taxonomy for recurring degradations (slow increase, step-change, seasonal regressions).
- Ship a lightweight orchestration pipeline that creates pre-populated initiative cards in Linear with evidence, severity, suggested remediations, and owner suggestions.
- Integrate with Console dashboards and the SLI ledger so each generated initiative links to the relevant telemetry, traces, and example requests.
- Provide an 'experiment cookbook' with 3 starter remediations (batch size tuning, KV cache prefix warmers, autoscaler policy adjustments) and measurable success criteria.
- Add rollout guard recommendations: automatic soft-throttle and canary thresholds for routes with recent SLO drift.

Out of scope: full automation of remediation (no auto-rollbacks without human approval) and replacing incident management tooling.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Drift classifier detects a multi-day SLI degradation pattern and surfaces a proposed initiative card in Linear with pre-filled title, description, telemetry links, and suggested owner.
2) Generated initiative includes at least one suggested experiment from the cookbook and a measurable success metric.
3) Console shows linked telemetry for the initiative (SLI timeseries + sample traces) and a one-click link to the initiative card.
4) On pilot with two product/engine teams, average time from drift alert -> assigned initiative <= 8 hours.
5) Rollout guard recommendations appear in the rollout dashboard for routes with active drift; teams can opt into soft-throttle policy.
proposal_summary: Implement a detection -> triage -> initiative creation flow: use existing SLI ledger queries to run a nightly drift analysis job, classify drift patterns, enrich with traces and request samples, and create a Linear card via API using templates. Provide an operator UI inside Console to review suggested initiatives, adjust severity, and dispatch. Start with pilot teams: Search and Hosted API.
implementation_plan:
1) Discovery (2 weeks): interview 5 on-call engineers and 4 PMs to validate classifications and cookbook entries.
2) Detection prototype (3 weeks): nightly job that flags drifts and stores evidence.
3) Initiative templating (1 week): create Linear API template and mapping rules.
4) Console integration (3 weeks): link telemetry and add review UI.
5) Pilot (4 weeks): enable for Search and Hosted API teams, collect metrics.
6) Rollout (2 weeks): expand to all serving teams and add rollout guard opt-in.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: classifier spams teams with false positives -> Mitigation: conservative thresholds + human-in-the-loop review UI
Risk: initiative noise overloads backlog -> Mitigation: auto-squash duplicates and add priority scoring by customer impact and burn rate
Risk: telemetry gaps for certain routes -> Mitigation: implement lightweight request sampling for identified routes
Risk: teams opt out of rollout guards -> Mitigation: provide clear KPIs and successful pilot case studies
